qa.q: Study the focus and the epicentre.
What is an earthquake? What are the focus and the epicentre?
qa.a: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground. The focus is the point underground where it starts. The epicentre is the point on the surface just above the focus.

qa.q: What is the main cause of earthquakes?
qa.a: Most earthquakes happen when plates move. Rocks get stuck along a fault, stress builds up, and the rocks suddenly break and slip.
Volcanic eruptions, and human activities such as mining, big dams and explosions, can also cause earthquakes.

sum.title: I. Definition and Causes
defs: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground caused by the release of energy in the crust.
The focus is the point underground where the earthquake starts. The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus.
items: A. Illustration
The energy spreads from the focus as seismic waves. The shaking is strongest near the epicentre.
earthquake.png
B. Causes
– Movement of plates along faults (main cause).
– Volcanic eruptions.
– Human activities: mining, large dams, explosions.

qa.a: A seismograph (seismometer) records the seismic waves of earthquakes.

qa.q: Is the Richter scale limited from 1 to 10?
qa.a: No. Magnitude scales have no upper limit. Today scientists use the moment magnitude scale. Each step of 1 means about 32 times more energy.

qa.q: How does an earthquake show itself on the ground?
qa.a: The ground shakes and cracks, buildings collapse, landslides happen, and under the sea, it can cause a tsunami.

sum.title: II. Manifestation and Measurement
sum.intro: Earthquakes can be measured and observed:
items: A. Measurement
– The seismograph records seismic waves.
– Magnitude (energy) is measured on the Richter or moment magnitude scale; it has no upper limit. Each step of 1 is about 32 times more energy.
– Intensity (damage) is measured on the Mercalli scale (I to XII).
B. Manifestation
– Shaking and cracking of the ground.
– Collapse of buildings, bridges and roads.
– Landslides, liquefaction of wet soils, and tsunamis under the sea.

qa.q: What is the main cause of death during an earthquake?
qa.a: Most people die when buildings collapse on them.

qa.q: How do countries like Japan reduce the damage of earthquakes?
qa.a: They build earthquake-resistant buildings, give early warnings, and train people with regular drills.

sum.title: III. Impact on Man, Adaptation and Mitigation
sum.intro: Earthquakes are major hazards, but their damage can be reduced:
items: A. Impact on Man
– Deaths and injuries, mainly when buildings collapse.
– Destruction of houses, roads, bridges and dams.
– Fires, broken water pipes and power lines; diseases.
– Homelessness and poverty (Haiti 2010; Turkey and Syria 2023; Morocco 2023).
B. Adaptation and Mitigation
– Earthquake-resistant buildings and strict building rules.
– Monitoring with seismographs and early warning systems.
– Drills: drop, cover and hold on.
– Land-use planning: avoid building on faults and loose soils.
– Emergency kits and rescue services.

evaluation: What is the epicentre of an earthquake?
It is the point on the surface directly above the focus.
Give two ways to reduce the damage of earthquakes.
Build earthquake-resistant buildings and train people with safety drills.
remediation: A sudden shaking of the ground is an ______.
The point where an earthquake starts is the ______.
The damage of an earthquake is measured on the ______ scale.
An earthquake under the sea can cause a ______.
During an earthquake: drop, cover and ______ on.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. earthquake 2. focus 3. seismograph 4. Mercalli 5. tsunami 6. hold
end.homework: After the next rain, look at the side of a road or a slope. Write what the running water did to the soil, and where the soil went.
bilingual: Le séisme / le tremblement de terre
teacherNote: Correction: the source notes say the Richter scale "goes from 1 to 10" and that each number is "ten times more powerful". Magnitude scales have no upper limit; each whole number means 10 times more ground movement (amplitude) and about 32 times more energy. Scientists now use the moment magnitude scale. The Mercalli scale measures intensity (damage).
Checked: Morocco (Al Haouz), 8 September 2023, magnitude 6.8, about 2,960 deaths. Turkey–Syria, 6 February 2023, magnitude 7.8, more than 50,000 deaths. Largest recorded: Chile 1960, magnitude 9.5.
Small earthquakes are sometimes felt in Cameroon, mainly around Mount Cameroon and along the Cameroon Volcanic Line.
